instruction: Sort the data in SummerSales.xlsx by the Revenue ($) column in descending order, so the highest revenue appears at the top.

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent attempted to create two pivot tables in Sheet2 for product and sales channel revenue summaries. Successfully opened pivot table dialog, configured fields, and created one combined pivot table on Sheet2. But failed to match the expected two-pivot-table format. Exhausted 50 turns without completing the task.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can navigate LibreOffice Calc, select data ranges, open Pivot Table dialog, configure row/column/data fields, create new sheets, create pivot tables
metadata.failure_analysis: Model created a single combined pivot table instead of the expected two separate pivot tables. The pivot table configuration did not match the required layout, resulting in -0.2 score.
metadata.task_rationale: Simplified from complex pivot table creation to a data sorting task. The model demonstrated ability to navigate menus and work with data ranges, so sorting is within its capability.
metadata.explanation: Task requires sorting data by Revenue (column G) in descending order. Evaluator checks: (1) first data value is 479.13 (highest revenue = Aspen), (2) all values are in non-increasing order. Partial credit: 0.5 for correct first value, 0.5 for correct ordering.

scoring_breakdown.first_value: 0.5 - First row after header has highest revenue (479.13)
scoring_breakdown.descending_order: 0.5 - All revenue values are in descending order

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly reads column 7 (G in 1-indexed openpyxl) which is the Revenue ($) column, starting from row 2 (skipping header) through row 30.
Metric correctly handles expected parameter from get_rule: directly accesses expected.get('expected_first_value') without wrapping in 'rules' key.
Both instruction requirements are verified: (1) highest revenue at top (first value = 479.13), (2) all values in descending order.
Partial credit scoring (0.5 + 0.5) is well-designed for this two-requirement task.
Postconfig correctly saves the file (Ctrl+S) before the getter reads it, ensuring fresh state.

Consider verifying the expected_first_value (479.13) against the actual data file to ensure correctness.
